title: Initialization failure messages report the last completed phase, not the failing phase
reasoning: The phase list is appended only after each phase succeeds, but the exception handler formats the error using self._initialized_phases[-1]. If container initialization fails, the error says it failed at 'configuration'; if service initialization fails, it says 'container'; and if configuration fails, it says 'unknown'. This makes startup failures misleading and can send operators toward the wrong subsystem.
reproduction: Force _initialize_container() to raise after configuration succeeds. The resulting InitializationError message reports phase 'configuration' even though the container phase failed.
recommendation: Track the current phase before entering each phase, and use that current phase in the error message and log. Keep _initialized_phases only for rollback of completed phases.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included, and this requires asserting failure diagnostics for each initialization phase rather than only success or rollback behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add parameterized tests that force failures in configuration, container, and services phases and assert the InitializationError identifies the actual failing phase.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/core/bootstrap/coordinator.py phase tracking in initialize(), plus focused failure-diagnostic tests.
